Hi peeps, to me, this "ignored" concept is actually the utmost vital key to open a pandora box. That being said, i must say that the answer has been given in the article. Well, then, not trying to "give an answer when an answer not been given" here, neither to be vague, blurry, nor confusing, let us reinstate Edge's words:

A broken level does not mean an ignored level Just because a level breaks it does not mean it has been ignored. If we do not understand the difference between ignored and used up, then our analysis will never be consistent. For us to make this determination lets cast our mind back to what has been said about

2144

FLs. We know that for a FTR to be considered a FL price MUST hit the opposing first target. So, it’s only logical to also apply this to ignored levels. Meaning, if price hits an area, reacts and does not hit the opposing target, we can consider it an ignored area. Conversely, if price hits the area and bounces back to the opposing first target then it cannot be considered ignored.

Edge did put an alert: "If you are still unclear of what a FL is, please stop here and go back to the FL lesson.". That is if we are still confused.

Be patient, fellow traders

Sorry to jump like this into discussion, Astro. I had the same problem understanding the ignored levels but i think right now i know the answer to this one. Some masters can confirm, of course. Before you go looking for every LS/QM or whatever it is, you have to look into what that LS is a reaction to. If your point 1 is a reaction to something like 2, then your point A ( the iQM) it is very insignificant. If you don't get your scale right in cases like this, i think you can't expect running trades, but only just small bounces and that is alright for scalping. Another thing: you want for your bigger scale LS to ties in with lower scale MPLS. These are the best levels to trade from on a touch trade, so basically, that point 2 which is HTF thing, it could align perfectly with an MPL inside your B zone. In this case, if you want to TT your first target would be inside B, and after that you will hope to fill the symmetry with B and maybe with my bigger grey box. However, that bigger grey box could be a FL in making, but it have to reach a target first, so basically the retrace could go even lower, and there is a lot to ask if you want a symmetry with the entire box. Now lets say you want a trade at your point A, and that point is reaction to my point 2, could you TT on it? Well, it could be possible, but you have to manage your expectation, because you are in the middle of things. You have to be aware that A its in the middle of your pink LSK box, and that box it is just a reaction to box below 1 and the entire box below 1 is just a reaction to 2 so you have to look again in LTF to see what point 1 really engulfed inside box 2, and maybe you have to look and draw anther LS from inside 2. But what i would do if i will want to trade 2 is i would look for a small Piece of PA/LSK,MPL inside A which ties in best with red line from 1. If i would have a BSZ formed just above which didn't yet completed the symmetry with A, i would gladly take a scalp and see here and i will watch the PA, because i'm in the middle. However, i wouldn't not expect much more symmetry than A, so the upper side of A would be my final target here, o maybe, if things are good, i would even expect a symmetry with your pink box.

Well, then it's simple. An LS its an LS in a particular scale, but in most of the cases it is a FL in lower scale only. An ignored level is a a level which failed to create a symmetry. In your case, when price hit your LSK at QM1, why it didn't bounce back to point 2. If you wanted to trade at QM 1, and put a SL just above the LSK itself, your "first" maximum expectation would be a symmetry with your LSK, and the "second" maximum expectation would be to the point 2, so you can have a nice flag replicated to the right of it. Even if that symmetry didn't happened you could have a profitable trade from there because you still working in lower scales. But in higher scale, your QM 1 failed to hold price back to 2 so 1 it is an ignored level. Now you can trade it as a ignored level so A its a good iQM to trade from. Now, is it A a FL? Not in this scale but look on the second diagram on my picture. Its the same like yours, but i drawn some LTF things inside it. See how A breaks 3 and then, once it hit 4, which is the MPL of your bigger LSK, you can draw your FL A. So basically A it is a FL in lower scale and when price will retrace to A, you can try to fill in the first instance the flag A, and after that, maybe you will replicate again the flag between 3 and 4. Now, its your B a FL? In higher scale not, because it broke an unimportant level. (your LSK was just a to the 1-2 FL/LSK or whatever is it) but look in lower scale. Your LSK was a FL because it broke 5 which was a FL that holds price UP. When B broke your LSK and hit the next target (the point 6), you can draw the FL B. When price return to B you can try to trade at the MPL of it, hoping that in the first instance you can replicate the FL B, and after that you can try and replicate the flag 5-6 on the right side. And that's how history repeats itself. That's why forex is so hard, and that's why i think IF is a genius.
